notes: Codex full Welsh review 2026-10-18 applied: tisiodd (not tisianodd); the caf i grammar row now has a caf i example (Cai: 'Caf i bastai yno!', s157 edited); bydd ↔ short-form row now shows equivalent propositions; a7 explanation and table make clear that this chapter practises 1sg/2sg/1pl only (3sg forms such as daw exist); nodyn states that an object or verb-noun complement softens; frathu radical gloss fixed; extra accepted answers (A.a10, C.c2–c4); s125 'gwthio'n gryf'. Review-question verdicts (all accepted, none deferred): mixed af i / gwnaf i with spoken wna i ddim is defensible; doi di is a southern teaching form (Sylfaen y De); cei di + VN for permission is natural; Ei di'n gyntaf is right; ffêr is feminine and ei ffêr e is correct; gwnaf i ddweud is natural; tasai dewrder gyda ti is grammatical; mor fawr â chychod is natural.

Short future: the four irregulars are productive in 1sg, 2sg and 1pl (af i/ei di/awn ni; gwnaf i/gwnei di/gwnawn ni; caf i/cei di/cawn ni; dof i/doi di/down ni), with wna i ddim and the yes-answers Af / Gwnaf. Regular -af (cymeraf i, gwelaf i, gwasgaf i) appears only in Rhita's boasts, glossed '= bydda i'n …', receptive. No 3sg short future is used: third persons keep bydd (Bydd Pero'n dod; Fydd e ddim yn marw), which Pensum A a7 contrasts.
Written affirmatives keep -f (gwnaf i, af i, as in the plan); the negative follows the plan's spoken wna i ddim. Pensa accept both gwnaf/gwna and wna/wnaf. See review question on s_wna1.

Promotions at 37: mor … â used productively (mor wyn â'r eira, mor fach â llygoden, mor fawr â thŷ, mor uchel â tharanau, mor fach ag wy); the other conditional persons used (baset ti, basech chi, basen ni, basen nhw).
Dafi's one deliberate error (Gwnaf i mwg) contrasts with the SM after the short future and is corrected in the next line by Mali (Gwnaf i fwg).
No open-slot words: neb (Pennod 26) and llawer (Pennod 32) are already introduced by parallel writers' open slots and are recycled here.

Continuity choices: the summit party is Arthur, Cai, Mali, Dafi and Pero; Myrddin climbs part-way, refuses to use magic ('Chi sy'n mynd i'r copa, dim fi') and arrives only after the cairn is built. The shepherd's rope comes from Pennod 36's hut. Cai wears Modlen's wool beard (34) and Rhita blows it away. Mali recovers the lock of Cynyr's beard (33). The giant is not killed: he falls on the summit, sleeps, and is buried asleep under a cairn (sets up the sleeping-king image of 40).

Continuity audit 2026-10-18 applied: Dafi climbs the beard cloak to the giant's head instead of flying (he cannot fly that high); Mali cuts Cynyr's lock from the cloak with the scissors she packed in 34; one-line army gag answers 33's threat of byddin o gewri (Cai: 'A ble mae dy fyddin di o gewri?' Rhita: 'Fi yw'r fyddin!'). New segments use ids from s201.
Cai's victory boast (s_boast) and his promise to tell the story in the Caerllion tavern, against Mali's 'Y stori go iawn', set up Pennod 38.
Known checker behaviour: phrase lexemes (ar fy mhen fy hun, gyda'n gilydd) may be reported against their component words; prose was not distorted to avoid it.

Recall pass 2026-10-18: in-place recurrences only (chapter is near its word ceiling): rhewi, dathlu, cynhesu. Gloss symbols: taflu ✋/🪨 → 'llaw → → → carreg'; ↓ removed from the clogwyn and baglu glosses.

Recall pass, pruning 2026-10-18 (docs/reviews/recall-pass-critique-2026-10-18.md): applied the critique's revert/rework rows (s150). Deleted new segments' IDs are retired, not to be reused; some recall targets deliberately left unmet rather than re-placed.

Owner fix 2026-11-04: Pensum C converted to eight open self_check questions in story order (Welsh rubrics in known words, key_terms, sources); the exact c2, c3 and c4 converted; 'Pam cwympodd y cawr?' (a four-reason rubric) and 'Beth fasai'n digwydd tasai'r cawr yn codi?' (unstated in the story) dropped; one Pam? (c1, s014 states it); c4 practises the short answer Af, c7 Gwnawn ni …; A ti? rubric without the unknown 'lle'. nodyn_en expanded to a full English explanation; the checker's 60-word cap is advisory (RULES §6). Unshown forms out of the grammar: dof i (title, rule_cy, grid), cawn ni and statement gwnei di (grid; the attested wnei di? stays), daw e (table row and A a7 feedback). Pensum B one answer each: b4 clogwyn, b5 buddugoliaeth.

Codex review 2026-11-04 (GPT-6.1-Sol, 37–40 half) applied: note narrows the mutation rule (noun objects and verb-nouns; ei keeps its own mutation) and no longer says the short forms take no verb-noun; 'two forms of dod'; Dafi's correction translated; recall A a10 now Gwnïodd Modlen y wisg → ei gwnïo (feminine ei gwneud never shown); C c4 asks for Mali's plan (… ei faglu e) instead of the bare Af; s091 gloss gives gwasgu's meaning at first use; unused brwydr out of the B bank. Optional fe variants added to finite A keys.

primary_new_grammar.label: Short-form future of mynd, gwneud, cael, dod: af i / ei di / awn ni; gwnaf i / gwnei di / gwnawn ni; caf i / cei di / cawn ni; dof i / doi di / down ni; wna i ddim; Wnei di …? — Gwnaf; SM after the short future (Gwnaf i fwg). Regular -af (cymeraf i, gwelaf i) and 3sg receptive.

cover.alt: The giant Rhita Gawr looms out of thick mist on the summit of Yr Wyddfa, his cloak of beards blowing, while Arthur, Cai and Mali, roped together, climb the last rocks below with old Pero.
cover.art_brief: The summit of Yr Wyddfa in thick grey mist (Eryri palette: mist greys, wet slate, a cold pale light). Looming out of the mist above, huge and only half visible, Rhita Gawr (match char-rhita.png: giant three times a man's height, bald dome, bushy black eyebrows, big red nose, his own long dark-brown beard, rough fawn tunic with rope belt, big brown boots) with his long cloak of stitched beard-tufts in red, black, grey and gold, with some slate-blue and brown (no faces), one long golden lock (Cynyr's beard) among them, stirring in the wind; vain smirk. Below him on a steep rocky path along a cliff edge: Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest; the crown hidden under his cloak, no crown visible) in front, Cai (15, tall, red-blond, rust-red tunic, red cloak, sword and round red shield) and Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, oatmeal-grey winter cloak, satchel and a cloth sack on her back) behind, all three tied together by one long brown rope; old Pero (shaggy black-and-white hound, grey muzzle) labouring up beside Arthur; a tiny red head with cream horns (Dafi) peeping from the sack. Far below, on a rock at the edge of the mist, the small figure of Myrddin (tall black brimmed hat) sits watching. Absolutely no text.

segments.text: Bore oer oedd hi yn Eryri: roedd y storm eira wedi mynd, ond roedd niwl llwyd, trwm ar yr Wyddfa, a doedd neb yn gallu gweld y copa.
Gadawodd Arthur, Cai, Mali a Myrddin fwthyn y bugail yn gynnar.
Roedd Pero'n cerdded yn araf wrth draed Arthur, ac roedd Dafi'n cysgu yn sach Mali, gyda'r bara.
Roedd rhaff hir, gryf gyda Mali hefyd: rhaff y bugail.

inference_aids.label: rhaff
inference_aids.art_brief: A long coil of rough brown shepherd's rope, knotted at one end. Ink line and watercolour, isolated on a plain flat white background (cut out to transparency afterwards), no text.

segments.text: "Af i'n gyntaf," meddai Cai.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Fi yw'r marchog, a fi yw'r cryfaf."
"Ei di'n gyntaf, Cai, ond ble mae'r llwybr?" meddai Mali.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Dw i ddim yn gweld dim byd yn y niwl."
"Awn ni gyda'n gilydd," meddai Arthur.
segments.speaker: char-arth

inference_aids.gloss: af i · ei di · awn ni

segments.text: "Af i gyda Cai, a doi di gyda ni, Mali, gyda'r rhaff."
"Bydd Pero'n dod hefyd, wrth gwrs."
Ond eisteddodd Myrddin ar graig wrth y llwybr, ac roedd ei het ddu'n wlyb yn y niwl.
"Af i ddim i'r copa," meddai e.
segments.speaker: char-myrddin

segments.text: "Dw i'n hen, ac mae'r llwybr yn serth. Bydda i'n aros yma, wrth y graig."
"Ond dewin dych chi!" meddai Cai.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Basech chi'n gallu taflu'r cawr i'r môr gyda hud!"
"Gallwn i," meddai Myrddin. "Ond wna i ddim."
segments.speaker: char-myrddin

segments.text: "Heddiw, does dim hud. Chi sy'n mynd i'r copa, dim fi."
Edrychodd e ar Arthur dros ei sbectol, ac roedd e'n gwenu. "Wyt ti'n cofio'r gwyddau?"
"Ydw," meddai Arthur. "Dylai brenin arwain fel gŵydd."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Gwnaf i rywbeth defnyddiol, felly," meddai Mali, a chododd hi'r rhaff ar ei chefn.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: Yn sydyn, daeth pen bach coch o'r sach, gyda bara ar ei drwyn.
"A fi?" meddai Dafi. "Beth wna i?"
segments.speaker: char-dafi

segments.text: "Cei di aros yn y sach, Dafi," meddai Mali.
segments.speaker: char-mali

inference_aids.gloss: caf i · cei di · cawn ni

segments.text: "Wna i ddim aros yn y sach!" meddai Dafi. "Mae'r bara wedi mynd!"
segments.speaker: char-dafi

segments.text: Dringodd y tri'n araf drwy'r niwl.
Doedd neb ar y llwybr, dim ond y tri ffrind a Pero.
Roedd y llethr yn serth, ac roedd creigiau wedi rhewi a cherrig rhydd ar y llwybr.
Weithiau roedd Cai'n cwympo ar ei drwyn, a weithiau roedd Pero'n eistedd i lawr ac yn edrych ar Arthur gyda llygaid trist.
Ar ochr y llwybr roedd clogwyn uchel, ac roedd niwl gwyn yn y cwm dan y clogwyn.

inference_aids.art_brief: A sheer grey crag dropping away into white mist, a narrow path along its top edge. Ink line and watercolour, isolated on a plain flat white background (cut out to transparency afterwards), no text.

segments.text: "Paid ag edrych i lawr, Mali!" meddai Cai.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Dw i ddim yn edrych i lawr," meddai Mali.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Ti sy'n edrych i lawr, Cai, ac rwyt ti mor wyn â'r eira."

segments.text: "Dw i ddim yn ofnus!" meddai Cai.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Wel… dw i ddim yn hoffi clogwyni."

Nawr roedd y tri ar yr un rhaff, ac roedd y clogwyn yn llai ofnadwy.
"Os bydd un ohonon ni'n cwympo, bydd y ddau ffrind yn dal y rhaff," meddai Arthur.
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "A Pero?" meddai Mali.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Mae pedair coes gyda Pero," meddai Arthur. "Dim ond dwy goes sy gyda ni."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: Ar ôl awr hir, clywon nhw sŵn o'r copa: llais mawr, dwfn, fel taran.
Roedd rhywbeth anferth yn canu yn y niwl, ac roedd y creigiau'n crynu.
"Pwy yw'r cawr mwyaf yn y byd? Fi!"
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: "Pwy yw'r cawr cryfaf yn y byd? Fi!"
"Pwy sy â'r clogyn gorau yn y byd? Fi, fi, fi!"
"Does neb yn fwy na fi!"
"Mae e'n canu amdano fe!" meddai Cai yn dawel.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Mae e'n falch iawn," meddai Mali. "Mae e mor falch â brenin."
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: "Awn ni i fyny'n dawel," meddai Arthur.
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Paid â thisian nawr, Dafi."
Ar y copa, roedd llai o niwl.
A dyna fe, ar garreg fawr: Rhita Gawr.
Roedd e'n anferth: roedd ei draed e mor fawr â chychod, ac roedd ei ben e yn y cymylau.
Roedd e'n gwisgo clogyn hir o farfau: barfau coch, barfau du, barfau llwyd a barfau aur.
Roedd e'n edrych ar ei glogyn ac yn gwenu fel plentyn gyda phastai.
"Mae e'n anferth!" meddai Cai yn dawel.
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Mae e'n fwy na'r neuadd yng Nghaerllion!"

inference_aids.alt: Rhita Gawr sits on a boulder on the misty summit of Yr Wyddfa admiring his long cloak sewn from many coloured beards, while Arthur, Cai and Mali, roped together, peer at him from behind a rock with old Pero; a little red dragon looks out of Mali's sack.
inference_aids.art_brief: The summit of Yr Wyddfa in thinning mist (Eryri palette: mist greys, wet slate, a little pale sky). Rhita Gawr (match char-rhita.png: giant three times a man's height, bald dome, bushy black eyebrows, big red nose, his own long dark-brown beard, rough fawn tunic with rope belt, big brown boots) sits on a great boulder, holding up a corner of his long cloak made of rows of stitched beard-tufts (red, black, grey and gold, with some slate-blue and brown; one long golden lock, Cynyr's beard; no faces) and admiring it vainly. In the foreground behind a wet grey rock: Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest; the crown hidden under his cloak, no crown visible), Cai (15, tall, red-blond, rust-red tunic, red cloak, sword and round red shield) and Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, oatmeal-grey winter cloak, satchel) tied together by one brown rope; old Pero (black-and-white shaggy hound, grey muzzle) crouching; Dafi (cup-sized red dragon, cream horns, yellow eyes) peeping out of a cloth sack on Mali's back. Even seated, the giant towers far above the children (his head about twice Arthur's height from the ground, matching a giant three times a man's height when standing), and his boots are as big as small boats. No text.

segments.text: "Dyma farf brenin Iwerddon," meddai'r cawr.
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: "A dyma farf brenin Llydaw. Mae llawer o farfau ar fy nghlogyn i. A dyma farf newydd: barf Cynyr, arglwydd Cwm Helyg! Barf hir, barf aur, barf dda!"
"Barf Dad!" meddai Mali yn dawel, ac roedd dagrau yn ei llygaid hi.
segments.speaker: char-mali

segments.text: Yn sydyn, cododd y cawr ei drwyn mawr coch ac arogli'r gwynt.

segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: Daeth Arthur o'r graig yn araf.
Roedd ei galon e'n curo, ond roedd ei lais e'n dawel.
"Arthur dw i," meddai e. "Fi yw'r brenin newydd."
segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: Rhuodd Rhita Gawr, a chwympodd cerrig bach i lawr y llethr.
"Ti? Y brenin newydd? Rwyt ti mor fach â llygoden!"
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: "Wel, frenin bach: cymeraf i dy farf di!
Gwelaf i hi ar fy nghlogyn i yfory!"
Plygodd e i lawr, ac edrychodd e ar wyneb Arthur am amser hir gyda'i lygaid bach.
"… Ond does dim barf gyda ti!"
Yna daeth Cai o'r graig hefyd, ac roedd barf wlân fawr ar ei wyneb e: barf ffug Modlen.
"Fi yw'r brenin!" meddai Cai yn uchel. "Dyma fy marf i!"
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: Edrychodd y cawr ar y farf wlân, ac yna ar wyneb coch Cai.
"Barf wlân? Barf ffug!" meddai Rhita. "Basai dafad yn gwybod hynny!"
segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: Rhuodd e eto, a hedfanodd y farf wlân i'r niwl.
"Fy marf i!" meddai Cai.
segments.speaker: char-cai

sections.title: Wna i ddim ymladd ar fy mhen fy hun

segments.text: Safodd Rhita Gawr ar ei draed, ac roedd ei ben e uwchben y niwl.

segments.text: "Ti a fi, frenin bach, ar dy ben dy hun!"

segments.speaker: char-arth

segments.text: "Dyn ni'n ffrindiau, ac awn ni i'r frwydr gyda'n gilydd."

segments.speaker: char-rhita

segments.text: "Llygoden, merch fach, hen gi a marchog heb farf!"

segments.speaker: char-arth

inference_aids.alt: Late afternoon on the summit: the children pile stones on the sleeping giant to make a cairn; Cai carries a big stone, Arthur and Mali smaller ones, Dafi brings a pebble the size of an egg, and Pero sleeps curled on top of the growing heap.
inference_aids.art_brief: The summit of Yr Wyddfa late in the day, the mist lifting into gold and grey light (Eryri palette). A long low cairn of grey stones covers the sleeping giant; only the tip of his big red nose and one big brown boot still show. Cai (15, tall, red-blond, rust-red tunic, red cloak) heaves a large stone, grinning; Arthur (12, untidy brown hair with a cowlick, freckles; plain blue cloak over a long blue robe with a small red dragon on the chest; the crown hidden under his cloak, no crown visible) and Mali (12, long dark braid, dark-blue dress, oatmeal-grey winter cloak) carry smaller stones; Mali has a folded bundle of the beard cloak at her feet. Dafi (cup-sized red dragon, cream horns) flies with a pebble no bigger than an egg towards the giant's nose. Old Pero (shaggy black-and-white hound) is curled asleep on top of the cairn. No one else is on the summit. No text.

segments.text: "Brwydr fawr, a buddugoliaeth fawr! Bydd y beirdd yn canu am y frwydr hon am flynyddoedd!"

segments.speaker: char-myrddin

segments.text: "Naddo," meddai Arthur. "Wnaethon ni ymladd gyda'n gilydd: Dafi, Pero, Mali, Cai a fi."

segments.text: Gwenodd Myrddin, ond doedd e ddim yn dweud dim byd.
Nawr doedd dim niwl, ac o'r copa roedd y plant yn gweld y byd: y mynyddoedd a'r llynnoedd, y môr a'r ynysoedd, fel y map ar wal tŵr Myrddin.
Yn bell yn y de, dan y cymylau, roedd Cwm Helyg.
"Pryd awn ni yn ôl i Gaerllion?" meddai Cai. "Dw i eisiau bwyd. Caf i bastai yno!"
segments.speaker: char-cai

segments.text: "Yfory," meddai Arthur. "Awn ni yn ôl yfory, gyda'n gilydd."

grammar.nodyn_en:
This chapter teaches a short way to talk about the future for three very common verbs: mynd ('go'), gwneud ('do, make') and cael ('get'), and for two forms of dod ('come'). Each short form means the same as the bydd forms you know: af i = bydda i'n mynd ('I'll go'), gwnaf i = bydda i'n gwneud ('I'll do, I'll make'), caf i = bydda i'n cael ('I'll get'). The verb itself carries the future, so there is no yn.

These are the forms the story uses, for 'I', 'you' (ti) and 'we':
- mynd: af i, ei di, awn ni. Af i'n gyntaf ('I'll go first'), says Cai. Mali answers: Ei di'n gyntaf, Cai, ond ble mae'r llwybr? ('You'll go first, Cai, but where is the path?'). Arthur decides: Awn ni gyda'n gilydd ('We'll go together').
- gwneud: gwnaf i, wnei di? (a question), gwnawn ni. Gwnaf i rywbeth defnyddiol, felly ('I'll do something useful, then'), says Mali; Gwnawn ni garnedd ('We'll make a cairn'), says Arthur.
- cael: caf i, cei di. Caf i bastai yno! ('I'll get a pie there!'), says Cai.
- dod: doi di, down ni. Af i gyda Cai, a doi di gyda ni, Mali ('I'll go with Cai, and you'll come with us, Mali'); Down ni o'r graig gyda'n gilydd ('We'll come out from the rock together').
For he, she or a noun, this chapter still uses bydd: Bydd Pero'n dod hefyd ('Pero will come too'); Fydd e ddim yn marw ('He won't die').

A noun object or a verb-noun straight after a short form takes the soft mutation: Gwnaf i fwg ('I'll make smoke'; mwg → fwg); Cei di frathu'r cawr ('You may bite the giant'; brathu → frathu); gwnawn ni wthio ('we'll push'; gwthio → wthio); Caf i bastai (pastai → bastai). Dafi makes this chapter's deliberate mistake: Gwnaf i mwg mawr iawn! Mali corrects him: Gwnaf i fwg, Dafi. Fwg! He repeats it correctly: Gwnaf i fwg mawr iawn ('I'll make very big smoke').

Gwnaf i has two uses. With a noun it means 'I'll make' or 'I'll do' (Gwnaf i fwg). With a verb-noun it simply makes a future, like bydda i'n: gwnaf i ei faglu e ('I'll trip him'), says Mali (here ei, 'him', brings its own soft mutation: baglu → faglu); A gwnaf i ysgrifennu'r stori ('And I'll write the story').

Cael also means 'may', as in Gaf i …? / Cei from Pennod 14, so cei di can mean 'you may': Cei di aros yn y sach, Dafi ('You can stay in the bag, Dafi').

To ask a question, the short form takes the soft mutation where it can: Dafi, wnei di fwg i fi? ('Dafi, will you make smoke for me?'). Ei di starts with a vowel, so it does not change: Mali, ei di at y clogwyn gyda'r rhaff? ('Mali, will you go to the cliff with the rope?'). When you are asked Ei di …? or Wnei di …?, you can answer with the verb alone, in the 'I' form: Mali answers Af ('Yes, I will [go]'), and the answer to Wnei di …? is Gwnaf. The same happens after a question word: Beth wna i? ('What will I do?'), asks Dafi; Pryd awn ni yn ôl i Gaerllion? ('When will we go back to Caerllion?'), asks Cai. Notice that before i the f of gwnaf is often dropped: wna i.

The negative uses the soft-mutated form and ddim: Wna i ddim aros yn y sach! ('I won't stay in the bag!'); Wna i ddim ymladd ar fy mhen fy hun ('I won't fight on my own'). Af i stays af i, because it begins with a vowel: Af i ddim i'r copa ('I won't go to the summit'), says Myrddin. Be careful not to confuse wna i ddim ('I won't') with the past wnes i ddim ('I didn't'): Wnest ti ddim ennill, a wnes i ddim ennill ar fy mhen fy hun ('You didn't win, and I didn't win on my own').

Ar fy mhen fy hun means 'on my own', literally 'on my head myself'; pen takes the nasal mutation after fy. For 'you' it is ar dy ben dy hun: Ti a fi, frenin bach, ar dy ben dy hun! ('You and me, little king, on your own!').

The chapter also compares with mor … â ('as … as'). Mor gives the soft mutation (though not to ll- and rh-), â gives the aspirate mutation, and before a vowel â becomes ag:
- Rwyt ti mor fach â llygoden! ('You're as small as a mouse!'); roedd e mor gryf â'i dad ('he was as strong as his father').
- Cododd Rhita garreg mor fawr â thŷ ('Rhita lifted a stone as big as a house'); gyda sŵn mor uchel â tharanau ('with a noise as loud as thunder'); roedd ei draed e mor fawr â chychod ('his feet were as big as boats').
- carreg mor fach ag wy ('a stone as small as an egg').

Finally, the conditional from Pennod 34 now has all its persons: baset ti ('you would'), basen ni ('we would'), basech chi ('you would', plural or polite) and basen nhw ('they would'). Rhita sneers: Baset ti'n ymladd ar dy ben dy hun, tasai dewrder gyda ti! ('You would fight on your own, if you had courage!'); Cai tells Myrddin: Basech chi'n gallu taflu'r cawr i'r môr gyda hud! ('You could throw the giant into the sea with magic!'). Arthur answers Cai's worry: Basen nhw'n chwerthin, ond basen ni'n ennill ('They would laugh, but we would win').
